6 x 3 ft mats in rows, 1 ft edge clearance, gaps 2/1.5/1 ft never below 1 ft, hand-laid nudge and turn kept only where clear of neighbors; count in [ceil(full/3), floor(2 full/3)], thinned evenly.
decisions.why: Unchanged in substance; serves the GM's aim that the drawn mats read as mats.

decisions.summary: The nudge and turn salted per yard; the turn up to 10 degrees where the neighbors leave room.
decisions.why: Unchanged; a degree of the hand-laid convention.

decisions.summary: Of equal counts, the lattice whose SEATED mats' box sits nearest the yard's center; an equal-count smaller lattice competes.
decisions.why: A placement choice among layouts that seat the same number; it changes no count and narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: A yard that physically cannot hold a third at a 1 ft gap draws as many as fit at it, at any size.
decisions.why: As ruled in round 5; on this round's own run the pool's six short yards are fit-limited against an exact search (arrangement-vertex enumeration on the exact inputs mat_cells received).

decisions.summary: 'Cannot reach a third at 1 ft' decided by the quarter-foot search, then solved exactly across and on a 0.02 ft grid down; SC-001's pool oracle a 0.02 ft grid anchored 0.01 ft off.
decisions.why: The across direction is now exact and the pool is right, but the down direction is still sampled at a fixed step, so the rule still lets off a yard that can hold more. On this round's own run, 1,000 synthetic yards of the roll's sizes (the pool's h/w and corner pull-ins, racks from rack_segment): a 25.41 x 17.52 ft yard with a rack draws 7 (third 9) where a 1 ft lattice seats 8 - _exact_lattice finds it at a 0.005 ft y step, and all 8 pass mat_cells' own fit test; its top row fits in a band under 0.02 ft tall below the rack's end. An exact down solve is possible and cheap (the arrangement's vertices: row edges meeting the rack's y limits k1 - mh - r*ph and k3 - r*ph, and pairwise crossings of the spots' outline constraint lines), so nothing makes the sampling necessary.

decisions.summary: The short-yard floor is four mats.
decisions.why: Bounds the exception; Inashiro's 20 x 14 ft yard seats 4 on the exact search and draws 4.

decisions.summary: Rack along a side edge inset 1 ft, near half preferred, off the yard's map-south half solved in map coordinates, whole-side fallback.
